name: Hiram
bio: Hiram was a skilled bronze craftsman from Tyre — son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali and a Tyrian father who had also worked in bronze — whom Solomon brought in to create the temple's bronze furnishings, a man "filled with wisdom, understanding and skill." He cast the two great bronze pillars that stood at the temple porch, eighteen cubits high, which he named Jachin and Boaz, along with their ornately decorated capitals of latticework and pomegranates. He also made the great bronze "Sea," a huge round basin resting on twelve bronze oxen, ten bronze movable stands with wheeled bases carved with lions, oxen, and cherubim, and the basins, shovels, and sprinkling bowls that went with them — vast quantities of bronze cast in the clay ground of the Jordan Valley between Succoth and Zarethan, so great in amount that its weight was never determined (1 Kings 7:13-47). Hiram the craftsman shares his name — but not his identity — with Hiram, king of Tyre, who supplied the temple's cedar and employed him.
